mcqs.q: A mandibular movement is defined as:
opts: Any movement of the lower jaw
Any movement of the lower jaw in which a condyle leaves its fossa
Any border movement reproducible on an articulator
Any movement of either jaw relative to the cranial base
mcqs.explain: The definition is deliberately broad — any movement of the lower jaw.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT one of the four stated reasons for studying mandibular movements?
opts: To determine the vertical dimension of occlusion
To understand occlusion
To arrange artificial teeth
To select and adjust articulators
mcqs.explain: The four reasons are understanding occlusion, arranging artificial teeth, understanding and treating TMJ problems, and selecting and adjusting articulators.

mcqs.q: Which statement about articulators and condylar movement is correct?
opts: No articulator can exactly duplicate the movements of the condyle
Fully adjustable articulators duplicate condylar movement exactly
Only an arcon articulator duplicates condylar movement exactly
Any articulator duplicates condylar movement once a face-bow record is mounted
mcqs.explain: No articulator can exactly duplicate the movements of the condyle; every instrument is an approximation.

mcqs.q: The three types of mandibular movement are:
opts: Rotation, translation and combination
Rotation, protrusion and retrusion
Opening, closing and lateral excursion
Hinge, glide and border movement
mcqs.explain: Rotation, translation and combination — the last accounting for most movements.

mcqs.q: Of the three types of mandibular movement, which accounts for MOST movements?
opts: Combination
Rotation
Translation
They occur in equal proportion
mcqs.explain: Most movements are a combination of rotation and translation; pure forms are the exception.

mcqs.q: Rotation is defined as the movement of a body:
opts: Around an axis
In the same direction and at the same rate
Against a fixed resistance
Through a fixed arc of 12 degrees
mcqs.explain: Rotation is movement of a body around an axis.

mcqs.q: Translation is defined as the movement of a body:
opts: In the same direction and at the same rate
Around an axis fixed in space
Forward only, never backward
At a rate proportional to the distance from the condyle
mcqs.explain: Translation is movement of a body in the same direction and at the same rate.

mcqs.q: In pure TRANSLATION of the mandible, the points of the jaw move:
opts: Simultaneously, in the same direction and at the same rate
Sequentially, beginning with the condyles and ending at the incisors
In the same direction but at rates proportional to their distance from the condyle
In opposite directions on the working and non-working sides
mcqs.explain: Every point in the mandible moves simultaneously in the same direction and at the same rate.

mcqs.q: From which position are PURE HINGE movements possible in opening and closing?
opts: Centric relation
Centric occlusion
The rest position
Maximum intercuspation
mcqs.explain: From a position of centric relation, pure hinge movements are possible in opening and closing.

mcqs.q: During a hinge movement, the condyles:
opts: Rotate within the glenoid fossa
Translate down the articular eminence
Move medially within the fossa
Rotate while shifting bodily to the working side
mcqs.explain: In a hinge movement the condyles rotate within the glenoid fossa.

mcqs.q: Rotation occurs within which joint space?
opts: The lower joint space
The upper joint space
Both spaces equally
Neither — it occurs outside the capsule
mcqs.explain: Rotation or hinge movement occurs within the lower joint space.

mcqs.q: Pure rotation occurs within what amount of mouth opening?
opts: The first 12 mm
The first 20 mm
The first 5 mm
The first 25 mm
mcqs.explain: Rotation occurs within the first 12 mm of opening of the mouth.

mcqs.q: When the measured distance between the maxillary and mandibular incisors EXCEEDS 12 mm, the condyles undergo:
opts: Combined rotation and translation
Pure translation only
Pure rotation only
Rotation on the working side and no movement on the balancing side
mcqs.explain: Beyond 12 mm of interincisal opening, the movement becomes combined rotation and translation.

mcqs.q: Translation occurs within which joint space?
opts: The upper joint space
The lower joint space
The retrodiscal space
The inferior capsular recess
mcqs.explain: Gliding or translation occurs in the upper joint space of the TMJ.

mcqs.q: Translation is said to occur whenever:
opts: A condyle leaves the glenoid fossa
The mandible rotates about the hinge axis
The teeth come into contact in centric occlusion
The lateral pterygoid relaxes
mcqs.explain: Translation occurs whenever a condyle leaves the glenoid fossa.

mcqs.q: Which movement is given as the model example of translation, and why?
opts: Protrusion, because both condyles translate together
Lateral excursion, because the working condyle rotates
Opening within 12 mm, because the condyles stay in the fossa
Retrusion, because the condyles return to the fossa
mcqs.explain: In protrusion both condyles translate, making it a good example of pure translation.

mcqs.q: In protrusion, which structures move in the same direction and at the same rate?
opts: The teeth, the condyles and the rami
The condyles and the discs only
The rami and the coronoid processes only
The teeth and the discs only
mcqs.explain: The teeth, condyles and rami all move in the same direction and at the same rate.

mcqs.q: In protrusion, both condyles:
opts: Leave their respective fossae and move down their eminences
Rotate within their fossae without leaving them
Move medially while rotating
Move backward and upward within the fossa
mcqs.explain: Protrusion carries the mandible forward with both condyles leaving their fossae and travelling down their eminences.

mcqs.q: Protrusion and retrusion are classified as:
opts: Translatory movements
Rotational movements
Combination movements
Border movements that are neither rotation nor translation
mcqs.explain: Protrusion and retrusion are both translatory movements.

mcqs.q: Which pairing of joint space and movement is CORRECT?
opts: Upper joint space — gliding; lower joint space — hinge
Upper joint space — hinge; lower joint space — gliding
Upper joint space — rotation; lower joint space — translation
Both spaces permit only translation
mcqs.explain: Gliding or translation occurs in the upper joint space, while rotation or hinge movement occurs in the lower joint space.

mcqs.q: The HORIZONTAL reference plane is described as:
opts: Parallel to the occlusal plane or the floor
Perpendicular to the occlusal plane
Best described by facing the patient
Also known as the side view
mcqs.explain: The horizontal plane is parallel to the occlusal plane or the floor.

mcqs.q: The FRONTAL reference plane is best described by:
opts: Facing the patient
Viewing the patient from the side
Viewing the patient from above
Viewing the patient from behind at eye level
mcqs.explain: The frontal plane is best described by facing the patient.

mcqs.q: The SAGITTAL plane is also known as:
opts: A side view
A frontal view
A superior view
An occlusal view
mcqs.explain: The sagittal plane is also known as a side view.

mcqs.q: The WORKING side is defined as:
opts: The side toward which the mandible moves
The side away from which the mandible moves
The side bearing the greater occlusal load in centric
The side on which the condyle translates furthest
mcqs.explain: The working side is the side toward which the mandible moves.

mcqs.q: During a lateral movement, the condyle on the WORKING side:
opts: Stays in its fossa, rotates and moves laterally
Leaves the fossa and moves forward and medially
Remains completely stationary within the fossa
Moves backward and laterally out of the fossa
mcqs.explain: The working side condyle stays in its fossa, rotates and moves laterally.

mcqs.q: The NON-WORKING side is also called the:
opts: Balancing side
Functional side
Rotating side
Centric side
mcqs.explain: The non-working side — the side opposite the working side — is the balancing side.

mcqs.q: During a lateral movement, the condyle on the BALANCING side moves:
opts: Forward, down the eminence, and medially
Forward, down the eminence, and laterally
Backward, up the eminence, and medially
Laterally within the fossa while rotating
mcqs.explain: The balancing side condyle leaves the fossa and moves forward down the eminence, and medially.

mcqs.q: Which condyle remains within its fossa during a lateral excursion?
opts: The working side condyle
The balancing side condyle
Both condyles
Neither condyle
mcqs.explain: The working side condyle stays in its fossa; the balancing side condyle leaves it.

mcqs.q: The Bennett angle is seen in which plane?
opts: The horizontal plane
The sagittal plane
The frontal plane
The occlusal plane of the working side only
mcqs.explain: When seen in the horizontal plane, the angle between the midsagittal plane and the curve of the non-working condyle is the Bennett angle.

mcqs.q: The Bennett angle lies between:
opts: The midsagittal plane and the curve of the non-working condyle
The midsagittal plane and the curve of the working condyle
The occlusal plane and the path of the balancing condyle
The Frankfort plane and the articular eminence
mcqs.explain: It is the angle between the midsagittal plane and the curve of the NON-WORKING condyle.

mcqs.q: Bennett's movement is defined as:
opts: Bodily movement of the mandible during lateral excursive movement, on the working side
Rotation of the non-working condyle about a vertical axis
The forward glide of the balancing condyle down its eminence
The downward and backward shift of the mandible in retrusion
mcqs.explain: Bennett's movement is the BODILY movement of the mandible during lateral excursion, occurring on the WORKING side.

mcqs.q: Bennett's movement is named after a dental surgeon of which nationality, and of which era?
opts: British, 1870–1947
American, 1890–1965
mcqs.explain: Sir Norman Godfrey Bennett, British dental surgeon, 1870–1947.

mcqs.q: Which pairing is CORRECT?
opts: Bennett angle — non-working side; Bennett movement — working side
Bennett angle — working side; Bennett movement — non-working side
Both are measured on the working side
Both are measured on the non-working side
mcqs.explain: The Bennett ANGLE belongs to the non-working (balancing) condyle; Bennett MOVEMENT occurs on the working side.

mcqs.q: Bennett movement is stated to be important in:
opts: Reproducing the cusps of artificial teeth
Determining the vertical dimension of rest
Selecting the shade of artificial teeth
Establishing the posterior palatal seal
mcqs.explain: Bennett movement is important in reproducing the cusps of artificial teeth.

mcqs.q: The amount of Bennett movement tends to:
opts: Increase as the occlusion becomes more mutilated
Decrease as the occlusion becomes more mutilated
Remain constant regardless of the state of the occlusion
Vary only with the steepness of the articular eminence
mcqs.explain: The amount of Bennett movement tends to increase as the occlusion becomes more mutilated.

mcqs.q: Compared with older groups who have lost teeth with subsequent tipping of the posterior teeth, young adults with good occlusion exhibit:
opts: Less Bennett movement
More Bennett movement
The same amount of Bennett movement
No Bennett movement at all
mcqs.explain: Young adults with good occlusion exhibit less movement than older groups who have lost teeth with subsequent tipping of the posteriors.

mcqs.q: The hinge axis is defined as an imaginary line:
opts: Between the mandibular condyles, about which the mandible rotates within the sagittal plane
Between the mandibular condyles, about which the mandible rotates within the frontal plane
Through the working condyle, about which the mandible shifts bodily
Joining the incisal point to the condyle on the balancing side
mcqs.explain: The hinge axis is an imaginary line between the mandibular condyles around which the mandible can rotate within the sagittal plane.

mcqs.q: Another name for the hinge axis is the:
opts: Transverse horizontal axis
Vertical axis of rotation
Sagittal condylar axis
Bennett axis
mcqs.explain: The hinge axis is also called the transverse horizontal axis.

mcqs.q: The transverse horizontal axis is the axis of rotation of the condyles during:
opts: The first 12 millimeters of mandibular opening
The whole range of mandibular opening
Protrusive movement only
Lateral excursion on the working side only
mcqs.explain: It is the axis of rotation of the mandibular condyles during the first 12 millimeters of mandibular opening.

mcqs.q: The hinge axis is most commonly transferred to a semi-adjustable articulator by means of:
opts: A face-bow
A protrusive wax record
A pantograph
A Gothic arch tracing
mcqs.explain: It is most commonly used for transfer to a semi-adjustable articulator by a face-bow.

mcqs.q: Which of the following best explains why a 12 mm interincisal opening is the critical figure in this lecture?
opts: It limits pure rotation and defines the transverse horizontal axis
It is the point at which the Bennett angle is measured
It is the width of the Bonwill triangle at the condyles
It is the fixed condylar guidance of a mean value articulator
mcqs.explain: Rotation occurs within the first 12 mm of opening, and the transverse horizontal axis is the axis of condylar rotation during those same first 12 mm.

mcqs.q: A patient who has lost several posterior teeth and whose remaining molars have tipped would be expected to show, relative to a dentate young adult:
opts: A greater amount of Bennett movement
A smaller amount of Bennett movement
An unchanged amount of Bennett movement
Loss of the hinge axis
mcqs.explain: The amount of Bennett movement increases as the occlusion becomes more mutilated — tooth loss and tipping remove the guidance that restrains the side shift.

saqs.q: Define mandibular movement and list the four reasons for studying mandibular movements.
saqs.a: A mandibular movement is ANY MOVEMENT OF THE LOWER JAW. They are studied to understand OCCLUSION, to ARRANGE ARTIFICIAL TEETH, to understand and treat TMJ PROBLEMS, and to SELECT AND ADJUST ARTICULATORS.

saqs.q: What fundamental limitation must be borne in mind when using any articulator?
saqs.a: NO ARTICULATOR CAN EXACTLY DUPLICATE THE MOVEMENTS OF THE CONDYLE. Every articulator is an approximation, so the clinician must understand the real movement in order to judge how far a given instrument's approximation can be trusted.

ans.text: No articulator can exactly duplicate the movements of the condyle. Every articulator is an approximation — so the clinician must understand the real movement in order to judge how far a given instrument's approximation can be trusted.

saqs.q: Name the three types of mandibular movement and define the first two.
saqs.a: ROTATION, TRANSLATION and COMBINATION, which accounts for most movements. ROTATION is the movement of a body AROUND AN AXIS. TRANSLATION is the movement of a body IN THE SAME DIRECTION AND AT THE SAME RATE — every point of the mandible moving simultaneously in the same direction at the same rate.

head: ROTATION
TRANSLATION
rows: the movement of a body around an axis
the movement of a body in the same direction and at the same rate — every point of the mandible moving simultaneously

saqs.q: Describe opening and closing from centric relation.
saqs.a: From a position of CENTRIC RELATION, PURE HINGE MOVEMENTS are possible in opening and closing. In a hinge movement, THE CONDYLES ROTATE WITHIN THE GLENOID FOSSA.

ans.text: From a position of centric relation, pure hinge movements are possible in opening and closing. In a hinge movement, the condyles rotate within the glenoid fossa.

saqs.q: Give four facts about rotation of the mandible.
saqs.a: (1) It is the PROCESS OF TURNING ABOUT AN AXIS. (2) It occurs when THE MOUTH OPENS AND CLOSES. (3) It occurs within the LOWER JOINT SPACE. (4) It occurs within the FIRST 12 mm of opening of the mouth.

list: The process of turning about an axis
Occurs when the mouth opens and closes
Occurs within the first 12 mm of opening

saqs.q: What happens when the mouth opens beyond 12 mm?
saqs.a: Opening and closing movements in which the distance between the maxillary and mandibular incisors is GREATER THAN 12 mm result in COMBINED ROTATION AND TRANSLATION of the condyles — the movement is no longer pure rotation.

ans.text: Once the measured distance between the maxillary and mandibular incisors is greater than 12 mm, the movement becomes combined rotation AND translation of the condyles — it is no longer pure rotation.

saqs.q: Give four facts about translation of the mandible.
saqs.a: (1) EVERY POINT in the mandible moves SIMULTANEOUSLY in the SAME DIRECTION and at the SAME RATE. (2) It occurs within the UPPER JOINT SPACE. (3) PROTRUSION is an example, in which BOTH CONDYLES TRANSLATE. (4) Translation occurs WHENEVER A CONDYLE LEAVES THE GLENOID FOSSA.

list: Every point in the mandible moves simultaneously, in the same direction and at the same rate
Protrusion is an example, in which both condyles translate
Occurs whenever a condyle leaves the glenoid fossa

saqs.q: Why is protrusion a good example of translation?
saqs.a: Because the TEETH, the CONDYLES and the RAMI all move IN THE SAME DIRECTION and AT THE SAME RATE — nothing rotates relative to anything else, which is exactly what defines pure translation.

ans.text: Because the teeth, the condyles and the rami all move in the same direction and at the same rate — nothing rotates relative to anything else, which is exactly what defines pure translation.

saqs.q: Define protrusion and retrusion and classify them.
saqs.a: PROTRUSION is when the mandible moves FORWARD and BOTH CONDYLES LEAVE THEIR RESPECTIVE FOSSAE and move DOWN THEIR EMINENCES. RETRUSION is the OPPOSITE PROCESS. Both are TRANSLATORY MOVEMENTS.

head: PROTRUSION
RETRUSION
rows: the mandible moves forward, and both condyles leave their respective fossae and move down their eminences

saqs.q: Which movement occurs in each joint space of the TMJ?
saqs.a: GLIDING OR TRANSLATION occurs in the UPPER joint space; ROTATION OR HINGE movement occurs in the LOWER joint space.

saqs.q: Name the three reference planes and state how each is described.
saqs.a: HORIZONTAL — parallel to the OCCLUSAL PLANE or the FLOOR. FRONTAL — best described by FACING THE PATIENT. SAGITTAL — also known as a SIDE VIEW.

head: Plane
Described as
rows: parallel to the occlusal plane or the floor

saqs.q: Define the working side and describe the behaviour of its condyle.
saqs.a: The WORKING SIDE is THE SIDE TOWARD WHICH THE MANDIBLE MOVES. When the mandible moves laterally, the condyle on the working side STAYS IN ITS FOSSA, ROTATES, and MOVES LATERALLY.

ans.text: The side toward which the mandible moves.

ans.h: Its condyle, in a lateral movement

saqs.q: Define the non-working side and describe the behaviour of its condyle.
saqs.a: The NON-WORKING SIDE is THE SIDE OPPOSITE THE WORKING SIDE. In a lateral movement, the balancing side condyle LEAVES THE FOSSA and moves FORWARD, DOWN THE EMINENCE, and MEDIALLY.

ans.text: The side opposite the working side — also called the balancing side.

ans.h: Its condyle, in a lateral movement

saqs.q: Define the Bennett angle.
saqs.a: When seen IN THE HORIZONTAL PLANE, an angle can be seen between the MIDSAGITTAL PLANE and the CURVE OF THE NON-WORKING CONDYLE. This angle is called the BENNETT ANGLE.

ans.text: Seen in the horizontal plane, the angle between the midsagittal plane and the curve of the non-working condyle.

saqs.q: Define Bennett's movement, and say who it is named after.
saqs.a: BODILY MOVEMENT OF THE MANDIBLE DURING LATERAL EXCURSIVE MOVEMENT, ON THE WORKING SIDE. It is named after Sir Norman Godfrey Bennett, British dental surgeon, 1870–1947.

ans.text: Bodily movement of the mandible during lateral excursive movement, on the working side. Named after Sir Norman Godfrey Bennett, British dental surgeon, 1870–1947.

saqs.q: Distinguish the Bennett angle from Bennett movement.
saqs.a: The BENNETT ANGLE is an ANGLE belonging to the NON-WORKING (balancing) condyle, seen in the HORIZONTAL plane between the midsagittal plane and the curve of that condyle. BENNETT MOVEMENT is a BODILY LATERAL SHIFT of the whole mandible, occurring on the WORKING side during lateral excursion.

head: BENNETT ANGLE
BENNETT MOVEMENT
rows: a bodily lateral shift of the whole mandible
the horizontal plane, between the midsagittal plane and the curve of that condyle

saqs.q: Why is Bennett movement clinically important, and what makes its amount vary between patients?
saqs.a: It is IMPORTANT IN REPRODUCING THE CUSPS OF ARTIFICIAL TEETH. Its amount tends to INCREASE AS THE OCCLUSION BECOMES MORE MUTILATED: young adults with good occlusion exhibit LESS movement than older groups who have lost teeth with subsequent TIPPING OF THE POSTERIOR TEETH.

ans.text: It is important in reproducing the cusps of artificial teeth.

head: Patient group
Amount of Bennett movement
rows: Older groups who have lost teeth, with subsequent tipping of the posterior teeth
more — the amount increases as the occlusion becomes more mutilated

saqs.q: Define the hinge axis and give its alternative name.
saqs.a: The HINGE AXIS is an IMAGINARY LINE BETWEEN THE MANDIBULAR CONDYLES around which the mandible can rotate WITHIN THE SAGITTAL PLANE. It is also called the TRANSVERSE HORIZONTAL AXIS.

ans.text: An imaginary line between the mandibular condyles around which the mandible can rotate within the sagittal plane. Also called the transverse horizontal axis.

saqs.q: State the range over which the transverse horizontal axis operates and how it is used clinically.
saqs.a: It is the AXIS OF ROTATION OF THE MANDIBULAR CONDYLES DURING THE FIRST 12 MILLIMETERS OF MANDIBULAR OPENING. It is MOST COMMONLY USED FOR TRANSFER TO A SEMI-ADJUSTABLE ARTICULATOR BY A FACE-BOW.

rows: the axis of rotation of the mandibular condyles during the first 12 millimeters of mandibular opening
most commonly used for transfer to a semi-adjustable articulator by a face-bow

saqs.q: Why does the figure of 12 mm appear twice in this lecture, and what links the two appearances?
saqs.a: Rotation occurs within the FIRST 12 mm OF OPENING, beyond which rotation and translation are combined; and the TRANSVERSE HORIZONTAL (hinge) AXIS is defined as the axis of condylar rotation DURING THOSE SAME FIRST 12 mm. They are the same fact seen twice: the hinge axis exists only while the movement is still pure rotation, which is why the hinge axis record must be taken at a small opening.

head: Where 12 mm appears
What it says
rows: occurs within the first 12 mm of opening — beyond which rotation and translation are combined
defined as the axis of condylar rotation during those same first 12 mm

ans.text: They are the same fact seen twice — the hinge axis exists only while the movement is still pure rotation, which is why the hinge axis record must be taken at a small opening.
